compare.intro: Ask two questions: what comes before the form (a noun such as 予想, or a verb in the dictionary form), and whether the sentence ends with the form or goes on after it. Then ask what it says: the best thing, the only way left, a better choice, a degree, a better word, the opposite, no room for something, or a result against expectations.

forms.tag: できればそれがいい · best if you can
forms.ja: 引っ越しの荷物は少ない{に越したことはない}。
forms.en: When you move house, the less you have to carry, the better.

forms.tag: いちばん · nothing is as … as
forms.ja: 自分の家{ほど}落ち着く場所{はない}。
forms.en: There is no place as relaxing as your own home.

forms.tag: いやなことより · rather than
forms.ja: うそをつく{くらいなら}、何も言わないほうがいい。
forms.en: Rather than tell a lie, it is better to say nothing.

forms.tag: ほかに方法がない · no choice but
forms.ja: 傘がないので、雨がやむのを待つ{よりほかない}。
forms.en: I have no umbrella, so there is nothing for it but to wait for the rain to stop.

forms.ja: 足が痛くて、一歩も歩けない{ほどだ}。
forms.en: My feet hurt so much that I can't take a single step.

forms.tag: 程度（小さくも） · so … that; only about
forms.ja: この町で知っている店は、駅前のコンビニ{くらいだ}。
forms.en: About the only shop I know in this town is the convenience store by the station.

forms.ja: あの店は、レストラン{というより}食堂だ。
forms.en: That place is more of a canteen than a restaurant.

forms.tag: 正反対・まして · far from; let alone
forms.ja: 休みの日なのに、休める{どころか}朝から家事に追われた。
forms.en: It was my day off, but far from resting, I was busy with housework from the morning.

forms.tag: 余裕がない · in no position to
forms.ja: 締め切りが明日なので、昼ご飯{どころではない}。
forms.en: The deadline is tomorrow, so lunch is out of the question.

forms.ja: 多くの人の予想{に反して}、その映画は大ヒットした。
forms.en: Contrary to what most people expected, the film was a big hit.

check.label: 転職したばかり
check.q: 新しい仕事に慣れなくて、趣味を楽しむ（　　）、ゆっくり眠る時間もない。
why: The bigger thing (enjoying a hobby) is out of the question, and even the smaller one (sleep) is missing: どころか … も.
どころではない ends the sentence. Here the sentence goes on after 、.
というより finds a better word for one thing. Hobbies and sleep are two different things.

drill.label: Choose the form
drill.q: 暑くなるという^専門家の予想^（　　）、今年の夏は^涼しい日が多かった^。
why: というより gives a better word for the same thing. A forecast and a cool summer are not two words for one thing.
どころか needs the opposite or a far stronger fact about the same thing. 予想どころか says nothing here.
A noun such as 予想 + に反して: the summer went against what the experts expected.
くらいなら follows a verb and leads to a better choice (〜ほうがいい). Nobody is choosing anything here.

drill.label: Choose the form
drill.q: メールの返事は^早い^（　　）^が^、夜中に送るのは相手に迷惑だ。
why: ほどだ needs an example of how far something goes, as in 驚くほどだ. 早い is the quality itself, not an example of its degree.
Fast is best, but (が) there is a limit: 〜に越したことはないが.
くらいなら needs a better choice after it (〜ほうがいい). It cannot stand before が.
よりほかない follows a verb in the dictionary form (待つよりほかない), not an adjective, and nothing here is the only way left.

drill.label: Choose the form
drill.q: 父が^急に入院した^ので、今は家族旅行（　　）。
why: よりほかない follows a verb in the dictionary form (待つよりほかない), and a trip is not the only way left.
ほどだ needs an example of a degree. 家族旅行 is not one.
家族旅行に越したことはない would say a family trip is best, which does not fit a father in hospital.
Noun + どころではない: the hospital stay leaves no room for a trip.

drill.label: Build the sentence
drill.hint: Nothing is as … as: X ほど, then the feeling, then はない. Which tile can sit right before はない?
drill.full: 旅先で道に迷ったとき{ほど}心細いこと{はない}。
drill.explain: 道に goes with 迷った, and 迷った describes とき. ときほど names the moment nothing beats, and 心細いこと sits right before はない.

drill.label: Choose the form
drill.q: このカレーは辛い（　　）、^しょっぱいと言ったほうがいい^。
why: The speaker finds a better word: not really spicy, more salty. と言ったほうがいい confirms the rewording.
どころか needs the opposite or a far stronger fact. Salty is neither the opposite of spicy nor a stronger kind of spicy.
ほどだ ends the sentence. Here the sentence goes on after 、.
に反して follows a noun such as 予想 or 期待, not an adjective.

drill.label: Choose the form
drill.q: ^忙しくて^、最近している運動は^駅まで歩くこと^（　　）。
why: ほどだ shows a high degree. It cannot say "only this much".
くらいだ can make something small: walking to the station is about all the exercise I get.
どころではない would say there is no room for walking, but walking is what I do.
というより needs a second, better word after it. Here the sentence ends.

drill.label: Choose the form
drill.q: ^最終のバスがもう出てしまった^ので、家まで歩いて帰る（　　）。
why: どころではない says something leaves no room to do it. The missed bus is a reason to walk, not a reason not to.
ことはない (met at N3) also ends in ない, but it means "there is no need to". With the last bus gone, walking is needed.
くらいなら needs a better choice after it. Here the sentence ends.
The last bus has gone, so walking is the only way left: よりほかない.

drill.label: Build the sentence
drill.after: いい物を一枚買ったほうがいい。
drill.hint: くらいなら sits right before the better choice. What does すぐに傷む describe?
drill.full: すぐに傷む安い服を何枚も買う{くらいなら}いい物を一枚買ったほうがいい。
drill.explain: すぐに傷む describes 服, so 安い服を comes first. 何枚も goes before 買う, and くらいなら follows the dictionary form, right before いい物を, the better choice.

exam.label: Choose the form
exam.q: 健康のためにジョギングを始めたが、体重は減る（　　）、三キロも増えてしまった。
exam.explain: Far from going down, my weight went up: どころか sets the fact against the opposite that was hoped for. だけでなく (met at N3) adds a second fact in the same direction, so 減るだけでなく … 増えた contradicts itself. に反して follows a noun such as 予想, and よりほかない ends a sentence.

exam.label: Choose the form
exam.q: 今度の部屋は日当たりがよく、冬でも暖房がいらない（　　）。
exam.explain: A high degree: the room is so sunny that even in winter no heating is needed. くらいなら needs a better choice after it, というより needs a second, better word after it, and に反して follows a noun such as 予想.

exam.label: Build the sentence
exam.full: 彼は両親の期待に反して{大学を}やめてパン屋を始めた。
exam.explain: 期待, に反して, 大学を, やめて. 両親の needs a noun, 期待, and に反して follows it. 大学を goes with やめて, which joins to パン屋を始めた.

scene.ja: 引っ越し業者の見積書
scene.intro: Tap every word you would check on the estimate before you book.

words.gloss: carrying things out (of the old home)
carrying things in (to the new home)

check.label: How the exam asks it
check.q: 業者と相談して、引っ越しの_日程_を来月の五日に決めた。
check.explain: 日程 is にってい. 日 is read ニチ, and becomes にっ before て, as in 日記 (にっき). 程 is テイ, as in 程度. じつ is the reading in 休日, and ひ the reading of 日 on its own.

skill.ask: Which plan meets all of this person's conditions at the lowest price?
skill.passage:
単身向け引っ越し料金の比較（同じ市内の場合）

A社「単身プラン」
料金：平日24,000円／土・日・祝日32,000円
大型家具・家電：2点まで無料（3点目から1点3,000円）
荷造り：お客様ご自身で（段ボール10箱まで無料）

B社「単身パック」
料金：27,000円（曜日による割増なし）
大型家具・家電：1点につき3,000円
荷造り：おまかせ可（別料金8,000円）

C社「単身プラン」
料金：平日20,000円／土・日・祝日26,000円
^※日曜日の夕方便（17時以降の搬出）は割増なし^
大型家具・家電：^1点につき3,000円^
荷造り：お客様ご自身で

※料金はすべて税込みです。
※見積もりは無料です。日にちが決まっていなくても、早めに取るに越したことはありません。
skill.strategy: Note the person's conditions first (Sunday, two large items, own packing, any time of day), then add up each plan line by line and read the ※ notes.

item.q: 会社員の森さんは、一人暮らしの部屋から同じ市内の部屋へ、日曜日に引っ越す。運ぶ大型の家電は冷蔵庫と洗濯機の二つで、荷造りは自分でする。時間は何時でもかまわない。料金がいちばん安いのはどれか。
options: C社の単身プランで、17時以降に搬出する
C社の単身プランで、17時より前に搬出する
item.explain: C社's note says a Sunday move with the things carried out after 17:00 has no surcharge, so the price is the weekday 20,000 yen. Two large items add 6,000 yen: 26,000 yen, the lowest.
why: There is no weekend surcharge, but each large item costs 3,000 yen: 27,000 + 6,000 = 33,000 yen.
Two large items are free, but the Sunday price is 32,000 yen.
Before 17:00 the weekend price applies: 26,000 + 6,000 = 32,000 yen.
